# handles

A handle a person types, made the one a service keeps: the white space at its ends dropped, each run of it inside made a hyphen and the letters made lower case, then held to what a handle is, each reason it is not said; and a tag, a handle and a number, read from text

#### `normalized`

```kn
fn normalized(raw: string) -> string
  raw.words().join("-").lower_ascii()
```

#### `problems`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn problems(handle: string) -> list[string]
  let n = handle.count()
  let short = if n < 3 then "shorter than 3 characters" else none
  let long = if n > 20 then "longer than 20 characters" else none
  let odd = if handle.chars().all(c => "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-".contains(c)) then none else "a character other than a to z, 0 to 9 and -"
  let start = if "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz".contains(handle.take(1)) then none else "not starting with a letter"
  let taken = if ["admin", "help", "root", "support"].contains(handle) then "a word the service keeps" else none
  [short, long, odd, start, taken].filter_map(x => x)
```

#### `handle`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn handle(raw: string) -> result[string, list[string]]
  let h = normalized(raw: raw)
  let why = problems(handle: h)
  if why.count() = 0 then ok(h) else err(why)
```

#### `tag`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn tag(text: string) -> result[Tag, list[string]]
  match text.index_of("#")
    none => err(["no # between the handle and the number"])
    some i =>
      let h = try handle(raw: text.take(i))
      match text.drop(i + 1).parse_number()
        none => err(["the number is not written in digits"])
        some n => if n >= 1 and n <= 9999 then ok(Tag { handle: h, number: n }) else err(["the number is not from 1 to 9999"])
```

## Examples

`kaname check` runs each line of `examples` in the reference interpreter, as a host would call the function, and compares the answer with the one written. The reference interpreter answers these.

```kn
normalized(raw: "  Ada   Lovelace ")
  = "ada-lovelace"
handle(raw: " Grace Hopper")
  = ok("grace-hopper")
handle(raw: "9")
  = err(["shorter than 3 characters", "not starting with a letter"])
handle(raw: "Root")
  = err(["a word the service keeps"])
tag(text: "Ada Lovelace#42")
  = ok(Tag { handle: "ada-lovelace", number: 42 })
tag(text: "ada#0")
  = err(["the number is not from 1 to 9999"])
```
